News Release
US data centre additions return to growth in Q2 2026 as developers push construction and pipeline continues to expand
54 GW added to Q2 pipeline, up 29% from year-ago and 5% from Q1 2026

28 October 2026
3 minute read

Email
Share by email

54 gigawatts (GW) of new data centre capacity was added to the US pipeline in Q2 2026, up 29% year-over-year, according to a new analysis from Wood Mackenzie.
Cumulative US disclosed data centre pipeline now totals more than 430 GW, of which approximately 59% is under active development. Projects totaling nearly 80 GW are currently under construction, up from 44 GW at the end of Q1, according to Wood Mackenzie’s US data center pipeline Q3 report.
This activity takes place against the backdrop of increased scrutiny and local opposition against data centres, which has triggered more than 400 data centre moratoriums since January 2026 from state and local lawmakers, affecting 18% of tracked data centre sites, representing more than 100 GW of planned capacity.
“The latest data reveals projects are steadily advancing from early development to permitting and construction phases,” said Caitlin Connelly, senior analyst, Wood Mackenzie. “However, power availability and local opposition will remain key constraints to near-term buildout.”
Development concentrates geographically…and among developers
Development is concentrating geographically, with PJM and ERCOT accounting for nearly half of all capacity under development. PJM has pushed ahead of ERCOT in total development capacity, with ~20 GW of new projects entering active development in H1 2026 alone. ERCOT's pipeline, meanwhile, appears to be the most mature, with more than 40% of its development capacity already under construction.
The top five developers account for a quarter of both planned and development capacity, and the pipeline is dominated by a relatively small number of large, sophisticated players. Capital concentration is even more pronounced, as total disclosed planned capex exceeds US$2.3 trillion nationally.
Utility Commitments Plateau
High confidence utility commitments levelled off at ~300 GW in Q2 2026, as a handful of utilities downgraded their reported pipelines to weed out speculative projects. Within that total, committed capacity with signed electricity service or construction agreements expanded to 201 GW, indicating that projects are progressing from advanced discussion phases to signed agreements. PJM remains most exposed to supply risk, with Wood Mackenzie’s risked supply view through 2036 running short of the market's high confidence load commitments.
Local Opposition Emerges as a Structural Constraint
Of the 400 data center moratoriums now spanning 42 states, the most significant single action is the September 2026 pause on new data centre permits in Texas and audit of the existing pipeline, which puts more than 60 GW of planned projects in Wood Mackenzie’s tracker under scrutiny.
Despite the increase in activity, which included just 45 such actions across 2023-2025, the picture is more nuanced than it appears, as 92% of moratoriums target land use or zoning approvals, with average durations of six to twelve months.
“We will likely continue to see local opposition, but the current moratoriums suggest that lawmakers are seeking time to develop stronger frameworks rather than moving to impose outright bans,” said Connelly.
Editor’s note:Q1 2026 additions have been revised upward to 52GW from the 36 GW reported at the time of our previous release, reflecting lags in disclosure tracking as project activity from that period continued to be captured. This revision is consistent with how pipeline data matures across reporting cycles, and does not alter the overall trend.
